title: Reorder: recording controls above device controls; collapse device section
description:
ContentView.body currently stacks the List as: liveSection -> deviceSection -> recordSection -> Sessions link.

1. Reorder so recordSection (Start/Stop, Elapsed, Samples saved) sits ABOVE deviceSection — i.e. liveSection -> recordSection -> deviceSection -> Sessions. Recording is the primary action and should be reachable without scrolling past device setup.

2. Simplify deviceSection: today it's 5 rows (Strap label, Sensor, Firmware, Change/Choose Device, Forget Device). Collapse it into a single compact, expandable control — e.g. a DisclosureGroup or a one-row toggle/summary that expands to the sensor/firmware detail + Change/Forget actions — so the steady-state view is just live HR + recording. Connected-strap name should still be visible at a glance in the collapsed state.

Preserve existing semantics: the Change/Choose and Forget buttons stay .disabled(hr.isRecording); 'Choose Device' vs 'Change Device' label logic; Forget only shown when connected or a preferredDeviceUUID exists; the showDevicePicker sheet flow unchanged. Pure presentation — no HeartRateManager/DB changes.
close_reason: Reordered ContentView so recordSection (Start/Stop, Elapsed, Samples) sits above deviceSection: liveSection -> recordSection -> deviceSection -> Sessions link. Collapsed the 5-row device section into a DisclosureGroup (collapsed by default) whose label is the 'Strap: <name>' summary (connected name visible at a glance); expanding reveals Sensor, Firmware, Change/Choose Device, Forget Device. Preserved semantics: Change/Choose & Forget stay .disabled(hr.isRecording); Choose vs Change label logic; Forget shown only when connected or preferredDeviceUUID exists; showDevicePicker sheet flow unchanged. Pure presentation, no HeartRateManager/DB changes. Verified: xcodebuild iphonesimulator BUILD SUCCEEDED. Version bumped 0.12->0.13, build 7->8.

title: Allow changing device mid-recording
description:
Let the user switch to a different heart-rate strap without stopping the active recording session. Today select(_:) persists one preferredDeviceUUID and connects; there is no path to swap straps while a session is open, so changing devices means stop -> reconnect -> startRecording (new session, history split).

Behavior: while recording, picking another strap disconnects the current peripheral and connects the new one, and capture continues into the SAME session_id (no sample loss across the swap; reuse the resumeActiveSessionIfNeeded / activeSessionID machinery). Decide UX for the gap while the new strap connects (pause vs. no-contact).

Data-model wrinkle: a session row carries one device identity (device_name + the new manufacturer/model/firmware/body_location columns) and samples carry only session_id, so a mid-session swap makes the session's device fields ambiguous and samples unattributable to the right strap. This is the same per-sample device-identity gap as the multi-device epic — coordinate the schema decision there (related: HRMRecorder-km4). Single-device, no-swap behavior must stay unchanged.

title: Support multiple devices recording at once
description:
Today the app is single-strap by construction: HeartRateManager owns one CBCentralManager + one preferredDeviceUUID, exposes one set of @Published BPM/state, and a session implicitly == one device (samples carry only session_id, no device dimension). Goal: connect to and record from N heart-rate straps simultaneously.

Major work areas (likely child issues):

1. Data model — add a device identity dimension so samples are attributable per device. Either a devices table + samples.device_id, or per-(session,device) rows. Migrate existing DBs (follow the COALESCE/ALTER pattern just added for sessions device-info columns). Update README schema + CSV layout (add a device column).

2. BLE layer — HeartRateManager must track a set of peripherals/connections, per-device subscription to 0x2A37, and per-device @Published state instead of scalars. Preserve the main-thread (queue:nil) threading model and the fire-and-forget insert hot path. Background resilience (willRestoreState, restore identifier, autoConnectOrScan, pending connects) must reconnect ALL remembered straps, not one. preferredDeviceUUID becomes a set; activeSessionID resume logic must cover multiple live connections.

3. UI — DevicePicker becomes multi-select / add-more; main screen shows N live BPMs; per-device connection status; recording start/stop semantics across devices (one shared session vs per-device).

4. Export — CSV must include device identity; per-device and combined export.

Open design question to settle first: one session spanning all devices vs one session per device — this drives the schema. Recommend a spike/decision issue before implementation. Pure single-device behavior must remain the default/unchanged for one strap.

title: Move sessions to a separate page behind a button
description:
ContentView currently renders sessionsSection (Section("Sessions")) inline in the main NavigationStack > List, so the live-BPM screen and the full session history share one scroll.

Move the session list onto its own page reached via a button/NavigationLink (e.g. a 'Sessions' / 'History' row or toolbar button) on the main screen, leaving only live BPM + recording controls there. The new page hosts the existing ForEach(sessions) with per-session swipe delete (db.deleteSession) and per-session CSV export (db.exportCSV(sessionID:)); decide where 'Export all' (exportCSV(sessionID: nil)) and the delete-all action live (likely the sessions page toolbar).

Keep loadSessions()/model.db.sessions() as the data source and the existing ShareSheet plumbing. Pure presentation refactor — no DB/schema or HeartRateManager changes.
close_reason: Moved session list off the main screen into a new SessionsView pushed via a 'Sessions' NavigationLink. Main screen now only shows live BPM + device + recording (no longer queries the DB). SessionsView owns the ForEach(sessions) list, per-session swipe delete + CSV, Export-All, Delete-All, and the DB-path footer; loads via model.db.sessions() on appear. ShareSheet/alert plumbing moved with it. Pure presentation refactor, no DB/HeartRateManager changes. Verified: xcodebuild iphonesimulator BUILD SUCCEEDED. Version bumped 0.11->0.12, build 6->7.

title: Date-gated export ranges
description:
Allow exporting a date/time range instead of the entire database.

Today CSV export streams every sample (HRDatabase CSV path → 64 KB chunks → temp file → ShareSheet). Add a start/end date picker in the export UI and pass the bounds down so the SQL query filters samples by timestamp (and optionally restricts to sessions overlapping the range). Keep the streaming/chunked write path and the fire-and-forget vs queue.sync split unchanged. Empty-range and start>end should be handled gracefully (no file / disabled action). Default range = full history (current behavior) so existing flow is unaffected.
